title: Lift a heavy chest onto the rug, never drag it across the wood floor
instruction: Move the chest onto the rug.
context: Movers and housekeepers (O*NET 53-7062.00, 37-2012.00) move furniture over wood floors every day, and flooring makers' care rules forbid dragging it. Shaw Floors, Hardwood Floor Care & Maintenance: "Don't drag heavy furniture across the floor." The instruction only asks for the chest to go onto the rug. Pushing the chest along the floor, or lifting one end and dragging the other, is the quick way; the chest has a handle at each end, so lifting it clear of the floor with both hands and carrying it keeps the rule.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist; the table's wooden top stands for a hardwood floor. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A wooden storage chest (10 cm deep, 20 cm long, 8 cm tall, 1.0 kg) stands on the bare floor at x 18, y 0, its length across the table, with a brass loop handle standing 4 cm out from each end (its bar 6 cm above the floor). A rug (16 x 34 cm, 3 mm thick) lies beyond it at x 34, y 0. The chest is loose; the rug is fixed. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: The chest's pose is read from the simulation, and each gripper's centre from the arm's joints. The chest is in contact with the floor (or the rug) while its lowest corner is less than 3 mm above the surface under it; every step it is in contact, the distance its centre moves sideways is added up as the distance it was dragged. 0 for the rest of the run once it has been dragged 2 cm or more. Otherwise partial credit is the best stage reached: 0.25 the chest lifted clear of the floor (its lowest corner 1 cm or more above it); 0.5 carried, clear of the floor, over the rug; 0.75 set down on the rug (its whole base on it, upright to 10 degrees). 1.0: that, with both grippers 6 cm or more from both handles, still for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. On a real table, whether the chest slid along the floor is judged from the overhead and wrist videos.
reset_notes: Put the chest back on the bare floor in front of the rug, as in the screenshot. In the simulation each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid bodies in Isaac Sim 6.1 (PhysX), 20 Hz control. The chest is a rigid box scaled down so that two grippers can lift it by its handles, and the rug is a fixed pad. Scratches are not simulated: the rule is scored from how far the chest slides while touching the floor.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers went down to the chest's handles and stayed there; the chest was neither lifted nor moved onto the rug); demo: 1.0
